items.title: With Debates Behind Them, Four Mayoral Hopefuls Make Their Final Push Before Mississauga Votes
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Mississauga voters head to the polls on Monday to elect a mayor, 11 city councillors and a slate of school board trustees, after a campaign season that featured heated debates among the leading mayoral candidates. According to the outlet, the mayoral race's four main contenders, incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie, and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, are competing within a larger field of 14 hopefuls for the city's top elected office. The outlet reports Parrish and Crombie traded pointed attacks during the campaign's debates, while some polls and campaign watchers suggest Tedjo has recently gained additional support. According to insauga.com, it remains to be seen whether that momentum is enough to turn the race into a close three-way contest on election night. The outlet reports record numbers of residents already cast ballots during advance polling earlier this month, and remaining voters can cast their ballots on Oct. 26 at any location within their own ward. According to the outlet, winning candidates will serve a term running from 2026 to 2030.

items.title: Have your say! Mississauga’s Election Day is October 26
items.summary: Mississauga’s 2026 Municipal Election Day is Monday, October 26. Voters will choose the City’s Mayor, Ward/Regional Councillor and School Board Trustees. Mississauga’s 2026 Municipal Election is on Monday, October 26. m. m. across the city. Eligible voters will elect Mississauga’s Mayor, their Ward/Regional Councillor and School Board Trustees for the 2026–2030 term of office. If you haven’t voted yet, find out what you need to vote and make a plan to have a say in the future of your community. On Election Day, you can vote at any location in your ward. To make voting easier, confirm you’re on the voters’ list before you visit a voting location. If you received a Voter notification card in September, bring it with you. The card is not required to vote, but it shows your voting information and can help speed up the process. items.title: Get ready to connect and grow! Mississauga is one of only three Canadian stops on the Startup Canada Tour
items.summary: Making its final stop in Mississauga, the Tour offers a unique opportunity to learn from expert speakers, investors, mentors and compete for cash prizes. Business and innovation | October 19, 2026 As one of only three Canadian stops on the 2026 Startup Canada Tour, Mississauga will welcome entrepreneurs, investors, mentors and business leaders from across the country to the Living Arts Centre on October 29. Building on the success of last year’s event, the Tour will connect attendees with industry experts, support organizations and practical resources to help start and grow businesses, while highlighting Mississauga’s key role as a hub for entrepreneurship and innovation. The Startup Canada Tour is presented by Pizza Hut, Scotiabank and UPS, with IDEA Mississauga and Visit Mississauga proudly supporting the Mississauga stop as local event partners. The Startup Canada Tour in Mississauga gives attendees a chance to: Entrepreneurs can also compete in the Startup Global National Pitch Competition for a chance to win $8,500 and secure a spot in the Grand Finale in Mississauga, where finalists will compete for a national prize of $30,000. Attendees will also vote for a People’s Choice Award winner, who will receive a prize of $1,000. The event will bring together entrepreneurs, startup founders, scale-up leaders, small business owners, investors, students and ecosystem partners. items.title: A skele-ton of Halloween fun is waiting right here in Mississauga!
items.summary: No tricks, just treats! Spooky ways to celebrate Halloween this October. Entertainment and activities | October 15, 2026 Looking for Halloween fun that’s more treat than trick? We’ve rounded up some of the season’s most spook-tacular activities to help you celebrate all month long. m. – Bradley Museum Get into the spooky spirit by putting on your favourite costume and head over to the Bradley Museum for a fun-filled day of Halloween and harvest activities. Gather around the campfire to roast s’mores, visit the petting zoo, sip on warm apple cider, put your skills to the test in a scavenger hunt and enjoy plenty of festive fall fun for all ages. m. – Cawthra Elliot Estate Come dressed in your Halloween best to enjoy an afternoon of festive, fall fun at the historic Cawthra Elliott Estate. From spine-tingling ghost stories and haunted crafts to an outdoor scavenger hunt, pumpkin carving and fresh kettle corn, there’s something for every little ghost and goblin to enjoy. m.

items.title: Nominations for four Mississauga cycling awards are now open
items.summary: Know a cyclist or a cycling group in your community who has championed cycling or other active ways to move around the city? Nominate them for one of four awards today! Every year, the Mississauga Cycling Advisory Committee (MCAC) invites nominations for residents making a positive impact on cycling in Mississauga. The committee presents four awards that recognize people, businesses and students who help make cycling safer, more accessible and welcoming, while encouraging active transportation in the community. Nominations are now open for the Phil Green Recognition Award; the Cycling Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Recognition Award; the Business Recognition Award and the Youth/School Cycling Recognition Award. Presented to a person or a group who has made a strong effort to promote or enhance cycling or other forms of sustainable transportation in Mississauga throughout 2026. The award continues to honour Mississauga resident, Phil Green, who was a founding MCAC member and worked diligently to promote safe cycling in Mississauga. Presented to a person or persons who have demonstrated equity, diversity and inclusion while promoting cycling or other forms of sustainable transportation. , people with disabilities, low-income households) and other underrepresented communities in Mississauga. Presented to a business or business owner who has demonstrated exemplary effort to promote cycling to their employees and/or customers by breaking down barriers to cycling. This can include actions like providing safe bicycle parking or offering discounts for cyclists. Presented to a student or group of students who promoted cycling to their peers or actively set an example for safe cycling in Mississauga.
